properties.content:
Report Details

Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety

Violation Code: 102.11(a)1 - GENERAL REQUIREMENTS – BMP AND DESIGN STANDARDS - Person failed to design, implement and maintain E & S BMPs to minimize the potential for accelerated erosion and sedimentation to protect, maintain, reclaim and restore water quality and existing and designated uses.
Violation ID: 992633
Permit API: 125-27073
Unconventional: No
County: Washington
Municipality: South Franklin Twp
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 4/19/2023
Comments: Today I conducted a routine inspection at the Varner 2 well. The access road was maintained and in good condition. The well head was maintain with no leaks or defects observed. Production tanks in good condition and were inside containment at the compressor station. No leaks or defects observed at the compressor stations equipment. The site is currently producing.During the inspection I discovered a slide on the Northside of the Varner 2 pad. The slip appeared to be a minor slide where the top soil slid off the slope. The size is approximately 40 feet in length x 15 feet in width. The slide exposed the slopes rock and dirt allowing for erosion. The well pads geo mat/ liner was also exposed at the edges. The slide appeared to be an old slide that settled and became stable. The area had thick vegetation and the landowner established a deer stand on the bench created by the slide. The well was spudded on 02/27/2014. The permit was issued on 08/09/2013 and expired on 08/09/2014. No waterway was impacted by the slide. The pipeline from the well head going to the compressor may be under the slide area. No pipe was exposed in the slide area so could not confirm the exact location of where the pipe was laid. The slide appeared to be just a surface slip with no deep scarp, so no immediate threat was observed at the time of inspection. No equipment or infrastructure are in the path of the slide.

Failure to install base of coal protective casing at least 30 feet below lowest workable coal seam and install at least two centralizers , one within 50 feet of casing seat and second within 100 feet of surface.
properties.content:
Report Details
Operator: Range Resources Appalachia Llc
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 2020-06-03
Violation Code: 78a83(g) - CASING AND CEMENTING - SURFACE AND COAL PROTECTIVE CASING AND CEMENTING PROCEEDURES - Operator failed to set and cement a coal protective string of casing thru workable coal seams. Failure to install base of coal protective casing at least 30 feet below lowest workable coal seam and install at least two centralizers , one within 50 feet of casing seat and second within 100 feet of surface.
Violation ID: 886183
Permit API: 125-27502
Unconventional: Yes
County: Washington
Municipality: West Finley Twp
Inspection Type: Administrative/File Review
Inspection Date: 2020-06-03
Comments: Based on the review of the well construction for the Thomas Greaves 7H well, the Department determined that the well was not drilled and cased in conformance casing and cementing requirements in the 2012 Oil and Gas Act (58 Pa. C.S. §§ 3201-3274) and 25 Pa. Code Chapter 78. The operator failed to segregate and protect the workable Pittsburgh coal seam by setting and cementing a coal protective casing across the workable Pittsburgh coal seam. The workable Pittsburgh coal seam was encountered from 670'-680'. Surface casing (13 3/8") is set at 378' and cemented to the surface. Intermediate casing (9 5/8") was set and cemented across the Pittsburgh coal seam. The intermediate casing set depth is 2107'. Intermediate casing cannot serve as coal protective casing.

Comments: On April 22, 2025, an administrative review was conducted in regard to the site restoration of the Sproul well site in Stewart Township, Fayette County. A Consent Order and Agreement (CO and A) was executed between the Operator and the Department for this site on 12/16/2021. According to the CO and A, the Operator has a schedule to restore the site upon placing the well into production or upon plugging the well. This along with the site having not yet achieved 70 percent uniform and adequate vegetative growth coverage during the time of IR 3957776 assert that the site has not been restored per the requirements of the 12/16/2021 CO and A.Therefore, violations continued in IR 3957776 shall remain outstanding.

Violation ID: 8178616
Permit API: 129-26206
Unconventional: No
County: Westmoreland
Municipality: Allegheny Township
Inspection Type: Complaint Inspection
Inspection Date: 3/06/2024
Comments: On March 6, 2024, inspection conducted in response to a complaint (CTS-374226) on the Terence Shaffer 1-P041 well in Allegheny Township, Westmoreland County. The following was observed:The well site was flooded by rainwater at the time of inspection (see photos 4 and 13). This did not appear to result in sedimentation on the well site during the time of inspection. The well site exhibited less than 70 percent vegetative growth coverage at the time of inspection. A gas odor was detected onsite. Hissing and bubbling was observed coming from the well head (see photos 2 and 3). The well API number and operator's information was posted on the meter box (see photo 6). However, the onsite posting lacked the operator's address. Little to no vegetative growth coverage was observed on the earthen berm surrounding the brine tank (see photos 7 and 8). A cotton-like substance was observed stuffed into one of the brine tank valves, with water flowing out of this valve (see photo 9). No elevated conductivity readings were detected underneath either brine tank valve, or anywhere onsite (see photos 5, 11, 12, and 14). Tire rutting that was severely eroded to bare stone was observed in the access road entrance (see photo 15). Sediment-laden pooling was observed in these ruts at a low point in the access road (see photo 16). An apparent stream or tributary flows through a culvert underneath this point in the access road. This sediment-laden pooling could be observed flowing from the access road ruts into this apparent stream/tributary at the culvert outlet, resulting in a discharge to the Waters of the Commonwealth (see photos 17 and 18). Department vehicles were not used to access the well site or access road for this inspection.The Department recommends that the operator post their address onsite, as is required by current regulations. OGI follow-up is being requested for evaluation of well integrity.Violations are being issued against the brine tank onsite, as it appears that it would fail to keep production fluids contained. Additional violations are being issued for failing to permanently stabilize the well site and access road, resulting in a sediment-laden discharge to the Waters of the Commonwealth.

Comments: On 4/11/2023, DEP representative John Rogers conducted an Administrative inspection on the Chesapeake Floydie well site. This inspection is to report the results of one water sample that was collected from a water/mud puddle east of the well heads.During an inspection on 3/8/2023, the department discovered high conductance fluid on the well pad surface outside of containment. The fluid covered a 20' x 60' area and field tested at 13.01 mS conductance with an Oakton PCTS-50 meter. The department collected water sample #9551-046 for laboratory analysis from location Lat: 41.66531 Long: -76.126427. On 4/4/2023 the department received the results of the laboratory analysis that shows elevated barium, strontium and lithium and is indicative of brine/production fluid being released onto the pad. The sample report is displayed in pictures 1 and 2. Chesapeake is pursuing Act 2 for the site in response to that incident.The release of fluid with elevated conductance to the pad surface constitutes violations of SWMA 301, CSL 402, 25 PA Code 78a.56(a) and 78.66(b)(2).Violations are still outstanding for inspection ID 3492400 for elevated conductance fluid being discovered on the unprotected pad surface and for inspection ID 3517302 for elevated conductance fluid being discovered on the unprotected pad surface.

Violation ID: 8166115
Permit API: 053-31042
Unconventional: No

Municipality: Howe Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 11/21/2023
Comments: This site is in the process of being constructed for a conventional well. The template for the well site has been completed. The well site location and access road have not been stoned. There has been no drilling activity on site and the pit has not been dug. There was no activity on site during the time of the inspection. The drilling permit and Erosion and Sedimentation (E and S) Plan were posted at the entrance of the location.The road leading to the well site location did not have culverts, sumps, or ditches installed as outlined in the E and S Plan. There were no temporary BMPs in place at the time of the inspection. Areas of earth disturbance associated with the construction of the well site location were not seeded and mulched.At the time of inspection, the site showed evidence of accelerated erosion. Sediment laden water was flowing parallel to the access road along the bottom slope of the constructed bank (pictured in Photo 1). The sediment laden water was ponding at the lowest point on the well site location (pictured in Photo 2). Stormwater and sediment from the well sites under construction up slope of Hastings SDT 47 OG Well were also contributing to the accelerated erosion at the site (pictured in Photo 3). Due to the volume of water, overflow from the low point was discharging off the site location (pictured in Photo 4). The sediment laden water was flowing through the woods directly discharging into Hastings Run (pictured in Photo 5). The operator, Steven Tachoir, was contacted over a voicemail to discuss the results of this inspection. He has been advised to install temporary BMPs to prevent accelerated erosion until the permanent BMPs can be installed in accordance with the E and S Plan. He has also been advised to seed and mulch the areas of earth disturbance associated with construction of the well. It has been proposed to the operator to meet on site to further discuss options for remediation. Follow up inspections will continue to occur until the work has been completed.

Unconventional: Yes

Inspection Date: 9/19/2023
Comments: This inspection was conducted in response to a notification from the operator that on 9/18/23 a leak was discovered in a GPU on Pad A which led to the release of an unknown quantity of produced fluid to the pad surface. I met with EQT representative Zac Subra upon arriving on Pad A. He showed me where the produced fluid leak occurred inside of GPU #3. He also showed me where the fluid overflowed the interior containment of the GPU and flowed outside of the GPU and onto the pad surface to the southwest of the GPU. A Waste Management crew was excavating the impacted area of the pad during this inspection. Mr. Subra said that the fluid appears to have traveled a couple of inches into the pad surface and then moved toward the southwest pad edge under the surface. A sump present in the stormwater channel along the southwest side of the pad had fluid in it with an electrical conductivity (EC) of 700 uS/cm. Mr. Subra stated that the initial EC reading taken in this sump was approximately 700 uS/cm and later it increased to approximately 1700 uS/cm. A smaller puddle of fluid approximately 25 feet to the north in the channel had an EC of 760 uS/cm during this inspection. No other fluid was observed in the channel or on the pad surface. The Department recommends vacuuming out the fluid in the southwest stormwater channel.Mr. Subra said that they plan to pursue Act 2 remediation due to the unknown volume of the release. Environmental consultant Penn E and R was present during this inspection. Mr. Subra said that Penn E and R were performing electrical conductivity screening and would take samples for the Act 2 remediation. Violations noted against permit 081-21855 for the produced fluid release to the surface of Pad A.Violations remain outstanding for the produced fluid release to Pad B from 2/6/23.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 11/06/2023 to K PETROLEUM INC in Somerset Township, Washington county. 78.54 - GENERAL REQUIREMENTS - Operator failed to control and dispose of fluids, residual waste and drill cuttings, including tophole water, brines, drilling fluids, drilling muds, stimulation fluids, well servicing fluids, oil, and production fluids in a manner that prevents pollution of the waters of the Commonwealth.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: K PETROLEUM INC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 11/06/2023
Violation Code: 78.54 - GENERAL REQUIREMENTS - Operator failed to control and dispose of fluids, residual waste and drill cuttings, including tophole water, brines, drilling fluids, drilling muds, stimulation fluids, well servicing fluids, oil, and production fluids in a manner that prevents pollution of the waters of the Commonwealth.
Violation ID: 8164679
Permit API: 125-22304
Unconventional: No
County: Washington
Municipality: Somerset Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 11/06/2023
Comments: On November 6 2023, the Department conducted an inspection of the Cole 1 OG Well in response to an OGI referral of the production tank leaking what appeared to be production fluid. At the time of inspection, the well appeared to drilled and equipped for production. The well tag was present on the well head. During the inspection, it appeared the production tank had previously been leaking at a valve near the bottom of the tank, but did not appear to be actively leaking. Distressed vegetation was observed in an approximate 3 foot radius around the tank. Directly below the valve, there appeared to be an excess amount of fluid along with a thick oil based matter. A background conductivity reading was taken and was 0.15 mS. Conductivity readings were taken in the soil in the area of the spill. The readings were elevated in comparison to the background reading with readings of 0.25mS, 0.45mS, 0.39mS, and 0.46mS. Elevated readings were detected in about a 3 foot radius around the production tank. Prior to leaving the location, the Department contacted KPI Representative Joel Greco to inform him of the release. Mr. Greco indicated that they had already replaced the faulty valve, and estimated the spill was roughly 15 barrels of production fluids and impacted the ground roughly 8 inches in depth. He stated remediation was scheduled to begin on 11/8/2023. I recommended that the Operator take immediate action to remediate the area in accordance with the Department's current spill policy. The Department requests clarification as to what caused the release, the quantity and type of fluid released (including the oil based matter) and how this was determined, as well as how long it is believed the release was occurring. Please include the clarification information within the NOV response.Based on today's inspection, violations are being issued for the failure to properly control production fluid (and/or other fluids) resulting in a release to the ground, as well as failure to report a release.

properties.content:
Report Details

Violation ID: 933603
Permit API: 081-21885
Unconventional: Yes
County: Lycoming
Municipality: McIntyre Twp
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 10/18/2021
Comments: Site inspection conducted to review residual waste processing activities at the EQT COP 551B pad with EQT Company Man Bill Mitchell. Weather at time of inspection is partly sunny and 46 degrees F. According to Mr. Mitchell, Precision Drilling Rig #110 is currently drilling the 6H well at a depth of 6378'. This is the 7th well of 9 total to be drilled during this setup. Drilling resumed on the 6H well on 10/15 and the well is being drilled using Water Based Mud to kickoff point at 8650' where the rig will be switched over to Synthetic OBM. The anticipated Total Depth of the 6H well is 22897'. All nine wells have been batch drilled to the intermediate depth. The 7H well was recently completed and cemented on 10/13. Clean Harbors Backyard Crew is processing the drill cuttings in the rig backyard. Three shale shakers and three drying shakers are active. Polymer flocculant is being added to the drilling mud during this inspection before it is run through the centrifuge. One centrifuge is removing cuttings from the drilling mud. An excavator is mixing wood pellets into the drill cuttings to solidify the material for landfill disposal. Prior to site transfer to EQT, ARD submitted a Request for Approval for Previously Approved Alternative Waste Management Practices (OG71) Form B for this well pad on 2/2/2021. The Department approved the request on 2/3/2021. The intent of onsite drill cuttings processing is to separate the solid fraction of the cuttings from reusable drilling mud fluid so fluids can be returned to mud tanks for further drilling activity. For further information, refer to the COP Tract 357 Pad A OG-71 Form A application regarding drill cuttings processing (EFACTS authorization #1300435). During this inspection, fluid with a sheen is observed within tertiary containment outside the OBM tanks. The Department recommends that containment structures be vacuumed and fluids be sent for treatment or disposal. The original trench sump collecting runoff along the access road near the mud tanks has a field conductivity reading of 733 uS/cm. There Re no new violations noted during this inspection. Violations remain outstanding on Pad B based on Inspection Report #3231577 by DEP WQS Brad Kline dated 8/9/21.

Comments: On 07/02/24 an incident inspection of the Walker 1 Well Site was conducted in response to the report of a spill received by the Department on 07/02/24. (CTS: 381922). Background:On 07/02/24 Greylock self-reported a brine release at the Walker 1 well. On 07/02/24 I spoke to Trevor Woods of Greylock to acquire additional details about the spill. During the inspection it was determined that an estimated 60 barrels of produced water had been released to the well area from a crack at the bottom of the poly tank being used on site. Investigation showed that the release was contained to the well area and no water ways were impacted. Remediation efforts were underway at the time of my inspection. Findings:-A well tag was observed on the well head (Photo #1).-The spill is suspected to have originated from a crack at the bottom of the tank (Photos #2-3).-Elevated conductivity was observed in the substrate in the spill area (Photos #4-9). -Crews were present on-site working to remediate the spill. (Photo #10). -No elevated conductivity was observed outside of the spill area.No discharge to surface water was observed. Violations of 78.57(a), SWMA 301, 91.34(a), and 78.54 are being issued for the release of brine to the ground.

Comments: The Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted a Follow-up inspection of Seneca's DCNR TR 007 PAD D site in Delmar Township, Tioga County on 3/1/2023 at 1300 hours. The weather was 34 degrees, cloudy, ice/snow mix, winds NNE @3mph. There were a total of eight wells onsite that appeared capable of production. Field conductivity of the puddles was measured between 230uS/cm and 830uS/cm. No fluid was observed in the production tank secondary containment. GPUs were all observed within adequate secondary containment. Stray pieces of secondary containment appear to have blown off the side of the well pad and are hung up on compost filter sock stakes.Violations of the following regulations are cited as OUTSTANDING against the DCNR 007 Pad D 229HU, API #117-22085: 25 Pa Code 78a.56(a)CSL 402(b)SWMA 301. An NOV response has not been received from the operator. No additional violations are noted at this time. I departed the site at 1515 hours.

Violations are being continued at this time for having inaccurate information on the well tag/posting. No fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed to be coming from or near the surface of the gas wellhead. At the time of this inspection, the Department observed a small production tank adjacent to the gas wellhead, no fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed to be coming from or near this tank. At the time of this inspection, the Department observed two other production tanks on site. The tank on the left was observed to be green and the tank on the right was observed to be a faded green color. No fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed to be coming from or near the surface of the green (left) production tank on site, however, the faded green (right) production tank was observed to have several corroded pipes connected to it. Towards the top of the faded green (right) production tank, the Department observed an area where severe corrosion caused piping to break off. This broken pipe was observed to be on the ground at the base of the production tank. No active fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed to be coming from or near this broken pipe, from the other corroded pipes still connected to the production tank, or the production tank at the time of this inspection. Violations are being continued at this time for failure to remove production equipment not in use from the gas well site. Report Details

Violation Code: CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
Violation ID: 8235154
Permit API: 015-23892
Unconventional: Yes
County: Bradford
Municipality: Troy Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 5/27/2025
Comments: Incident Inspection of Repsol's "Broadleaf Holdings" Marcellus well site. Tory Rogers called the DEP on Friday morning May 23, 2025 to report a release of approximately 9 gallons of diesel based drilling mud released from a flare stack to the pad surface that morning. I met with Tory Rogers, Jim Brown, Megan DePue (all 3 Repsol), and Scotty Brown (DEP, OGI) on site. While drilling a future Marcellus Shale well there was a control issue, so they lit the flare stack to burn off natural gas incurred. Some drilling mud blew out of the flare stack, estimated at 7 gallons onto pad containment, and 9 gallons on the pad surface. Rogers showed us where the flare stack released drilling mud. Resource Environmental directed excavation to remove pad material the drilling mud impacted, which was approximately a 10'X60' area. They completed the cleanup around 1600 hrs the same day the release occurred. The material is in 2 dumpsters on the NE corner of the pad. I got a 1.5 ppm reading with a 10.6 eV MiniRae photoionization detector (PID) from the removed pad material, and a 0.0 ppm PID reading from the remediated pad surface, which indicates the cleanup sufficiently removed the impacted pad material. Drill cuttings in a dumpster near the drill rig gave a 135.7 ppm reading. Violations cited to the 015-23893 drilling permit are considered immediately corrected.Rogers explained they increased the density of the drill mud from 12.8 lbs/gal to 13.5 lbs/gal to provide more well control.Repsol laid the containment on this pad on February 26 thru March 3, 2025. Felt liner (130 mil thickness) went down first, then wood/steel mats. Fine gravel is used to fill gaps between the mats.Precision Drilling 110 started drilling 4 new Marcellus wells at this site on April 1 2025, and expect to finish drilling around June 10, 2025. There are also 4 existing Marcellus wells here. They drill on water based mud for the vertical section, then switch to diesel based mud for the kickoff (curve) and horizontal section.Vegetation and rock stabilize soil of the site to comply with 102.22 Permanent Stabilization. I did not see accelerated erosion or sedimentation.Post Construction Stormwater Management (PCSM) controls are in place and appear to be functioning as designed. Containment structures are intact. I did not observe any leaks or other deficiencies. Pooled water on the pad surface in 3 separate puddles has electrical conductivity (EC) of 0.68-1.7 mS/cm with an Oakton PCTS5.62FJLP
